# input: 500ミリリットル + 500ミリリットル
# No number agreement of any kind: Japanese marks plurality nowhere, so every
# unit has one printed form and 1 and 5 take the same word. The separators are
# English's — "," for groups, "." for the decimal.
# No space between number and unit, on input or output, which is what makes
# the round trip hold: the engine reads back its own "2,000ミリリットル"
# The units are katakana loans, and the conversion markers are the case
# particles を (accusative, the source) and から ("from"), written glued to the
2リットルからミリリットル
# 立方メートル is one token, so Japanese prints the cubic metre in words where
# the Romance languages fall back to `m³`. 立米 is the clipped trade spelling
# and is read onto the same unit.
# The myriad. Japanese counts in ten-thousands, so 万 is its own magnitude word
# and 一万 is one of them rather than ten of a thousand.
# The word operators need whitespace around them even though Japanese is
# written without any: かける, 割る and 足す are matched as separate tokens.
# The katakana operator beside the native one — both are ordinary Japanese.
2リットル プラス 500ミリリットル
